damping-off.name: Damping-off
damping-off.cause: Pythium, Rhizoctonia and other soilborne pathogens
damping-off.early: Seedlings fail to emerge or develop a pinched, wet stem base.
damping-off.progress: Seedlings topple; gaps develop in nursery rows.
damping-off.conditions: Use clean nursery media and avoid saturated seedbeds.

powdery-mildew.name: Powdery mildew
powdery-mildew.cause: Powdery mildew fungi; species depend on the host
powdery-mildew.early: Small white, powdery patches appear on young leaves or shoots.
powdery-mildew.progress: Patches merge; leaves curl and flower or fruit quality may decline.
powdery-mildew.conditions: Crowded growth and humid canopies favour infection.

downy-mildew.name: Downy mildew
downy-mildew.early: Pale or angular patches appear on leaves.
downy-mildew.progress: Grey-purple growth may develop underneath; affected leaves dry.
downy-mildew.conditions: Prolonged leaf wetness and dense canopies favour spread.

early-blight.name: Early blight
early-blight.cause: Alternaria solani and related Alternaria species
early-blight.early: Brown, target-like spots begin on older leaves.
early-blight.progress: Spots merge; lower foliage dries and fruit or tuber lesions may develop.
early-blight.conditions: Inspect older foliage after warm, wet weather.

late-blight.name: Late blight
late-blight.progress: Dark lesions spread rapidly; white growth may occur at lesion edges in humidity.
late-blight.conditions: Cool, wet conditions favour rapid spread.

fusarium-wilt.name: Fusarium wilt
fusarium-wilt.early: Lower leaves yellow; wilting may begin on one side.
fusarium-wilt.progress: Vascular tissue browns and wilting becomes persistent.
fusarium-wilt.conditions: Check roots and stems; drought and other wilts can look similar.

verticillium-wilt.name: Verticillium wilt
verticillium-wilt.early: Lower leaves yellow, sometimes in wedge-shaped areas.
verticillium-wilt.progress: Progressive wilting and vascular discoloration weaken the plant.
verticillium-wilt.conditions: Soilborne infection can persist across seasons.

bacterial-wilt.name: Bacterial wilt
bacterial-wilt.early: Leaves wilt while much of the foliage is still green.
bacterial-wilt.progress: Wilting becomes permanent; cut stems may show bacterial ooze.
bacterial-wilt.conditions: Use laboratory confirmation to separate bacterial and fungal wilts.

bacterial-spot.name: Bacterial leaf and fruit spot
bacterial-spot.cause: Xanthomonas species; identity varies with crop
bacterial-spot.progress: Spots darken and merge; some hosts develop raised fruit lesions.
bacterial-spot.conditions: Rain splash and handling wet plants can spread bacteria.

bacterial-canker.name: Bacterial canker
bacterial-canker.early: Leaf edges scorch and plants may wilt unevenly.
bacterial-canker.progress: Stem cankers and small bird-eye fruit spots may develop.
bacterial-canker.conditions: Inspect transplants and avoid spreading sap on tools.

anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
anthracnose.early: Small dark spots appear on leaves, stems or developing produce.
anthracnose.progress: Lesions enlarge and may become sunken; fruit decay can intensify after harvest.
anthracnose.conditions: Wet weather and wounded or ripening produce favour symptoms.

alternaria-spot.name: Alternaria leaf spot
alternaria-spot.early: Small dark leaf spots may show concentric rings.
alternaria-spot.progress: Spots merge and affected leaves yellow or dry.
alternaria-spot.conditions: Inspect lower and older leaves after wet periods.

cercospora-spot.name: Cercospora leaf spot
cercospora-spot.early: Small, distinct leaf spots develop pale or brown centres.
cercospora-spot.progress: Numerous spots reduce green leaf area and may cause leaf fall.
cercospora-spot.conditions: Warm, humid canopies favour many leaf-spot diseases.

rust.name: Rust
rust.early: Yellow or pale flecks precede powdery orange or brown pustules.
rust.progress: Pustules multiply; leaves dry and grain or crop filling suffers.
rust.conditions: Check both leaf surfaces; rust species differ between crops.

grey-mould.name: Grey mould
grey-mould.early: Flowers or soft tissues develop tan, water-soaked spots.
grey-mould.progress: Grey fuzzy growth and soft decay spread on affected tissue.
grey-mould.conditions: Humid, poorly ventilated flowering canopies favour infection.

soft-rot.name: Bacterial soft rot
soft-rot.early: Wounded tissue becomes water-soaked and soft.
soft-rot.progress: Tissue collapses into wet decay, sometimes with a strong odour.
soft-rot.conditions: Avoid wounds, contaminated water and poorly ventilated storage.

root-rot.name: Root and collar rot
root-rot.cause: Soilborne fungi and fungus-like organisms; the causal agent varies by crop.
root-rot.early: Plants grow poorly; fine roots or the stem base discolour.
root-rot.progress: Roots decay and plants wilt or collapse.
root-rot.conditions: Check drainage and roots; waterlogging can cause similar symptoms.

sclerotinia.name: Sclerotinia stem rot
sclerotinia.early: Watery lesions appear around stems or branches.
sclerotinia.progress: White cottony growth and hard black resting bodies may develop.
sclerotinia.conditions: Inspect dense canopies during humid flowering periods.

charcoal-rot.name: Charcoal rot
charcoal-rot.early: Plants lose vigour and develop premature wilting.
charcoal-rot.progress: Roots or stems show numerous tiny black, charcoal-like structures.
charcoal-rot.conditions: Heat and moisture stress can intensify symptoms.

phytophthora-rot.name: Phytophthora root, foot or heart rot
phytophthora-rot.cause: Phytophthora species; host and affected organ vary
phytophthora-rot.early: Root or collar tissues darken; leaves lose vigour.
phytophthora-rot.progress: Roots, crown or central tissues decay; plants may collapse.
phytophthora-rot.conditions: Saturated soil and contaminated planting material favour infection.

mosaic.name: Mosaic virus diseases
mosaic.cause: Different host-specific viruses cause mosaic symptoms
mosaic.early: Leaves develop uneven light and dark green patterns.
mosaic.progress: Leaves may distort and plants remain stunted with reduced yield.
mosaic.conditions: Insect vectors or handling spread different viruses; identify the actual cause.

leaf-curl.name: Leaf curl virus disease
leaf-curl.cause: Host-specific begomoviruses, often transmitted by whiteflies
leaf-curl.early: Young leaves curl and show yellowing or reduced size.
leaf-curl.progress: Plants become stunted and set fewer flowers or fruits.
leaf-curl.conditions: Inspect young growth and whiteflies; curling alone is not diagnostic.

purple-blotch.name: Purple blotch
purple-blotch.early: Small pale lesions form on onion-family leaves.
purple-blotch.progress: Lesions enlarge into purple, zoned patches; leaves bend and dry.
purple-blotch.conditions: Leaf wetness and older or injured foliage favour infection.

stemphylium.name: Stemphylium leaf blight
stemphylium.early: Small yellow to brown leaf lesions appear.
stemphylium.progress: Lesions lengthen and merge, causing extensive leaf blight.
stemphylium.conditions: Wet leaves and damaged foliage favour infection.

basal-rot.name: Fusarium basal rot
basal-rot.early: Leaf tips yellow while basal roots discolour.
basal-rot.progress: The bulb base rots; decay can continue during storage.
basal-rot.conditions: Inspect basal plates and use sound planting bulbs or cloves.

white-rot.name: Allium white rot
white-rot.early: Onion-family leaves yellow and plants weaken.
white-rot.progress: White growth and tiny black resting bodies form around the bulb base.
white-rot.conditions: Do not move contaminated soil or planting material to clean beds.

black-scurf.name: Black scurf and stem canker
black-scurf.early: Sprouts or young stems develop brown cankers.
black-scurf.progress: Tuber surfaces develop hard black structures resembling attached soil.
black-scurf.conditions: Use clean seed tubers and avoid cold, waterlogged planting soil.

potato-scab.name: Common scab
potato-scab.early: Small corky spots form on developing potato tubers.
potato-scab.progress: Raised or pitted corky lesions enlarge on the tuber surface.
potato-scab.conditions: Check field history and moisture during tuber initiation.

clubroot.name: Clubroot
clubroot.early: Brassica plants wilt during the day and grow unevenly.
clubroot.progress: Roots become swollen and club-shaped; older galls decay.
clubroot.conditions: Avoid moving infested soil or transplants into clean fields.

brassica-black-rot.name: Black rot of brassicas
brassica-black-rot.early: Yellow V-shaped lesions begin at leaf margins.
brassica-black-rot.progress: Veins darken and lesions extend into leaves or heads.
brassica-black-rot.conditions: Inspect seedling health and avoid overhead splash on wet crops.

blast.name: Blast
blast.cause: Pyricularia / Magnaporthe species; host lineages differ
blast.early: Spindle-shaped leaf lesions develop pale centres and darker margins.
blast.progress: Neck or finger infection can interrupt grain filling and cause empty heads.
blast.conditions: Inspect nursery leaves, tillers and emerging crop heads.

rice-blight.name: Bacterial leaf blight of rice
rice-blight.early: Leaf tips or margins develop water-soaked yellow streaks.
rice-blight.progress: Long yellow-white lesions spread; severely affected foliage dries.
rice-blight.conditions: Inspect after storms and avoid spreading infected leaf material.

rice-brown-spot.name: Brown spot of rice
rice-brown-spot.early: Small oval brown spots appear on rice leaves.
rice-brown-spot.progress: Spots multiply and may affect glumes and grain quality.
rice-brown-spot.conditions: Nutrient stress and seed health should be checked along with infection.

sheath-blight.name: Sheath blight
sheath-blight.early: Oval green-grey lesions start on lower leaf sheaths.
sheath-blight.progress: Lesions spread upward and adjacent tillers become affected.
sheath-blight.conditions: Dense, humid canopies can favour spread between tillers.

rice-tungro.name: Rice tungro
rice-tungro.cause: Rice tungro virus complex, transmitted by leafhoppers
rice-tungro.early: Young rice plants show yellow-orange leaves and reduced growth.
rice-tungro.progress: Plants remain stunted, tiller poorly and produce fewer filled grains.
rice-tungro.conditions: Compare affected patches and inspect leafhopper activity.

false-smut.name: False smut of rice
false-smut.early: Individual developing grains are replaced by swollen fungal balls.
false-smut.progress: Balls turn yellow-orange, then green-black as spores mature.
false-smut.conditions: Inspect panicles during grain development; do not infer risk from photos alone.

smut.name: Smut diseases of cereals
smut.early: Affected heads or kernels develop abnormal swelling or darkening.
smut.progress: Grain or head tissues are replaced by dark spore masses.
smut.conditions: Use clean seed and identify the host-specific smut before treatment.

maize-blight.name: Turcicum / northern leaf blight
maize-blight.early: Long grey-green lesions begin on maize leaves.
maize-blight.progress: Cigar-shaped brown lesions expand and reduce green leaf area.
maize-blight.conditions: Inspect lower leaves after prolonged wet weather.

groundnut-leaf-spot.name: Early and late leaf spot of groundnut
groundnut-leaf-spot.early: Brown to dark spots appear on groundnut leaflets.
groundnut-leaf-spot.progress: Spots multiply; infected foliage yellows and drops prematurely.
groundnut-leaf-spot.conditions: Inspect both leaflet surfaces; early and late leaf spots differ.

sigatoka.name: Sigatoka leaf spots of banana
sigatoka.early: Small pale or dark streaks appear on banana leaves.
sigatoka.progress: Streaks enlarge into dead patches and functional leaf area declines.
sigatoka.conditions: Inspect recently unfurled leaves in humid conditions.

panama.name: Panama disease of banana
panama.cause: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense complex
panama.early: Older banana leaves yellow and droop around the plant.
panama.progress: Pseudostem vascular tissues discolour and the plant declines.
panama.conditions: Use clean planting material; strain identification requires specialist testing.

bunchy-top.name: Banana bunchy top
bunchy-top.early: Dark green streaks may occur on veins or petioles.
bunchy-top.progress: Short, narrow upright leaves crowd at the top and plants fail to yield normally.
bunchy-top.conditions: Inspect suckers and banana aphids; obtain confirmation before rouging.

citrus-canker.name: Citrus canker
citrus-canker.early: Small raised spots appear on citrus leaves or fruit.
citrus-canker.progress: Corky crater-like lesions develop yellow halos; severe infection causes leaf fall.
citrus-canker.conditions: Wind-driven rain and injured tissue favour spread.

citrus-greening.name: Citrus greening / HLB
citrus-greening.early: Leaves develop uneven, asymmetric blotchy mottling.
citrus-greening.progress: Shoots decline; fruits may be small, lopsided and poorly coloured.
citrus-greening.conditions: Distinguish from nutrient deficiency and seek diagnostic confirmation.

citrus-tristeza.name: Citrus tristeza
citrus-tristeza.early: Trees may show poor vigour or leaf yellowing.
citrus-tristeza.progress: Susceptible combinations decline or develop stem pitting.
citrus-tristeza.conditions: Use certified planting material; symptoms depend on rootstock and strain.

papaya-ringspot.name: Papaya ringspot
papaya-ringspot.early: Young leaves develop mosaic patterns and distortion.
papaya-ringspot.progress: Leaf blades narrow; fruit may show circular oily rings.
papaya-ringspot.conditions: Inspect young leaves and nearby aphids; photos do not confirm the virus.

apple-scab.name: Apple scab
apple-scab.early: Olive, velvety patches appear on young leaves or fruit.
apple-scab.progress: Lesions darken; fruit becomes scabby and may crack.
apple-scab.conditions: Wet periods around new leaf growth and fruit set favour infection.

fire-blight.name: Fire blight
fire-blight.early: Blossoms brown and young shoots begin to wilt.
fire-blight.progress: Shoots may form a hooked tip; cankers develop and affected growth blackens.
fire-blight.conditions: Inspect blossoms and young shoots; confirm before extensive pruning.

peach-leaf-curl.name: Peach leaf curl
peach-leaf-curl.early: Emerging leaves become puckered and reddish.
peach-leaf-curl.progress: Leaves thicken, distort and may drop early.
peach-leaf-curl.conditions: Cool, wet weather during leaf emergence favours infection.

brown-rot.name: Brown rot of stone fruit
brown-rot.early: Blossoms wilt or ripening fruit develops brown spots.
brown-rot.progress: Soft brown decay spreads; spore cushions and mummified fruit may form.
brown-rot.conditions: Inspect blossoms and damaged ripening fruit in wet weather.

grape-black-rot.name: Black rot of grape
grape-black-rot.early: Tan leaf spots or small brown berry lesions appear.
grape-black-rot.progress: Berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
grape-black-rot.conditions: Inspect foliage and young berries after rainy periods.

red-rot.name: Red rot of sugarcane
red-rot.early: Canes lose vigour and top leaves may yellow.
red-rot.progress: Split canes show red internal tissue interrupted by white patches.
red-rot.conditions: Inspect setts and declining stools; use clean planting cane.

coffee-rust.name: Coffee leaf rust
coffee-rust.early: Pale patches appear on the upper leaf surface.
coffee-rust.progress: Orange powdery pustules form underneath; affected leaves fall.
coffee-rust.conditions: Inspect leaf undersides, especially in humid canopies.

rose-black-spot.name: Black spot of rose
rose-black-spot.early: Dark, often fringed spots appear on rose leaves.
rose-black-spot.progress: Yellowing develops around spots and leaves drop prematurely.
rose-black-spot.conditions: Prolonged leaf wetness favours repeated infections.

sooty-mould.name: Sooty mould
sooty-mould.cause: Surface-growing fungi associated with insect honeydew
sooty-mould.early: A dark film develops on sticky leaves or fruit.
sooty-mould.progress: Black surface growth can cover large areas and reduce light reaching leaves.
sooty-mould.conditions: Look for sap-sucking insects producing honeydew.

blossom-end-rot.name: Blossom-end rot
blossom-end-rot.cause: Disrupted calcium supply to developing fruit, often linked to water stress
blossom-end-rot.early: A small water-soaked patch forms at the blossom end.
blossom-end-rot.progress: The patch becomes dark, sunken and leathery as the fruit grows.
blossom-end-rot.conditions: Check watering consistency and roots; this is not a contagious fungus.

aphids.name: Aphids
aphids.cause: Aphididae; species depend on the crop
aphids.early: Colonies gather on tender shoots, buds or leaf undersides.
aphids.progress: Leaves curl and honeydew attracts ants or sooty mould; some species transmit viruses.
aphids.conditions: Inspect new growth and protect natural enemies.

whiteflies.name: Whiteflies
whiteflies.early: Tiny white adults fly up when leaf undersides are disturbed.
whiteflies.progress: Nymphs, honeydew and leaf yellowing accumulate; some species transmit viruses.
whiteflies.conditions: Check leaf undersides, not only flying adults.

thrips.name: Thrips
thrips.cause: Thrips species; vectors differ by species
thrips.early: Leaves or petals develop pale, silvery feeding scars.
thrips.progress: Distortion, browning or corky scars increase; some thrips transmit viruses.
thrips.conditions: Tap flowers over a pale sheet and inspect young folded leaves.

spider-mites.name: Spider mites
spider-mites.early: Fine pale stippling appears on leaves.
spider-mites.progress: Bronzing, drying and fine webbing develop during heavy infestations.
spider-mites.conditions: Inspect leaf undersides with a hand lens, especially in dry conditions.

mealybugs.name: Mealybugs
mealybugs.early: White cottony insects cluster in sheltered plant parts.
mealybugs.progress: Honeydew, black surface mould and plant weakening increase.
mealybugs.conditions: Inspect leaf axils, fruit clusters and ant activity.

scales.name: Scale insects
scales.early: Small fixed shell-like or soft bumps appear on plant tissues.
scales.progress: Heavy colonies weaken shoots; soft scales may produce honeydew.
scales.conditions: Examine twigs and leaves closely; species identification matters.

leafminers.name: Leaf miners
leafminers.early: Thin winding mines appear within leaves.
leafminers.progress: Mines broaden or merge and reduce functioning leaf tissue.
leafminers.conditions: Hold a leaf against the light and inspect fresh mines.

leafhoppers.name: Leafhoppers / jassids
leafhoppers.early: Leaf edges yellow where small jumping insects feed.
leafhoppers.progress: Margins curl and scorch; severe feeding causes hopperburn.
leafhoppers.conditions: Inspect leaf undersides and avoid confusing adults with harmless insects.

fruit-borer.name: Fruit and pod borer
fruit-borer.early: Small feeding holes or damaged flower buds appear.
fruit-borer.progress: Caterpillars bore into fruit or pods, leaving holes and frass.
fruit-borer.conditions: Inspect flowers and developing produce; confirm the caterpillar species.

tobacco-caterpillar.name: Tobacco caterpillar
tobacco-caterpillar.early: Young larvae scrape leaves together near an egg mass.
tobacco-caterpillar.progress: Older larvae feed heavily, leaving irregular holes or extensive defoliation.
tobacco-caterpillar.conditions: Check lower foliage and field edges for young larval groups.

fall-armyworm.name: Fall armyworm
fall-armyworm.early: Young maize leaves show pale scraping and small holes.
fall-armyworm.progress: Ragged whorl damage and frass accumulate; larvae may attack ears.
fall-armyworm.conditions: Open the whorl carefully and distinguish from other armyworms.

cutworms.name: Cutworms
cutworms.early: Seedlings are cut or chewed near soil level.
cutworms.progress: Missing plants occur in patches; larvae hide in nearby soil by day.
cutworms.conditions: Check around freshly cut plants at dusk or early morning.

fruit-flies.name: Fruit flies
fruit-flies.cause: Tephritid fruit flies; species depend on crop
fruit-flies.early: Small punctures or sap marks appear on developing produce.
fruit-flies.progress: Maggots feed inside; fruit softens, rots or drops.
fruit-flies.conditions: Inspect fallen or prematurely soft fruit and identify the fruit-fly species.

diamondback.name: Diamondback moth
diamondback.early: Small pale leaf windows appear on brassicas.
diamondback.progress: Shot holes and damaged outer leaves or heads develop.
diamondback.conditions: Inspect undersides and folded leaves for small, wriggling larvae.

red-pumpkin-beetle.name: Red pumpkin beetle
red-pumpkin-beetle.early: Seedling leaves develop round feeding holes.
red-pumpkin-beetle.progress: Heavy adult feeding damages seedlings and flowers; larvae feed below ground.
red-pumpkin-beetle.conditions: Inspect emerging cucurbit seedlings and flowers.

brinjal-borer.name: Brinjal shoot and fruit borer
brinjal-borer.early: Tender shoot tips wilt or show an entry hole.
brinjal-borer.progress: Larvae tunnel in shoots and fruits, producing frass-filled holes.
brinjal-borer.conditions: Inspect wilted tips and recently set fruits.

okra-borer.name: Okra shoot and fruit borer
okra-borer.early: Tender shoots wilt after internal feeding.
okra-borer.progress: Flower buds and pods develop bore holes with frass.
okra-borer.conditions: Inspect shoot tips, buds and young pods.

rice-stem-borer.name: Rice yellow stem borer
rice-stem-borer.early: Central shoots wilt, producing dead hearts.
rice-stem-borer.progress: Later attack causes white, empty panicles that pull out easily.
rice-stem-borer.conditions: Inspect affected tillers and split stems to check for larvae.

rice-planthopper.name: Brown planthopper
rice-planthopper.early: Small brown insects gather near the base of rice tillers.
rice-planthopper.progress: Yellow-brown patches and hopperburn appear under heavy feeding.
rice-planthopper.conditions: Inspect lower stems, not just the leaf canopy.

rice-leaffolder.name: Rice leaf folder
rice-leaffolder.early: Leaves are folded lengthwise and held with silk.
rice-leaffolder.progress: White feeding streaks develop inside folded leaves.
rice-leaffolder.conditions: Open a fresh fold and check for a living caterpillar.

shoot-fly.name: Shoot fly
shoot-fly.early: Young central shoots wilt after internal larval feeding.
shoot-fly.progress: Dead hearts and poor establishment develop in affected seedlings.
shoot-fly.conditions: Inspect damaged seedlings and verify the crop-specific fly.

pink-bollworm.name: Pink bollworm
pink-bollworm.early: Flowers may form rosettes or young bolls show subtle entry marks.
pink-bollworm.progress: Pink larvae feed inside bolls and damage seeds and lint.
pink-bollworm.conditions: Inspect flowers and split sample bolls; outward symptoms can be limited.

mustard-aphid.name: Mustard aphid
mustard-aphid.early: Pale green aphids gather on inflorescences and tender shoots.
mustard-aphid.progress: Dense colonies stunt growth and reduce normal pod development.
mustard-aphid.conditions: Check flowering shoots and preserve ladybirds and other predators.

white-grubs.name: White grubs
white-grubs.early: Plants wilt or grow unevenly as roots are eaten.
white-grubs.progress: Root loss causes patchy plant death or poor anchorage.
white-grubs.conditions: Inspect root zones near affected plants and identify the grub.

root-knot.name: Root-knot nematodes
root-knot.early: Plants are stunted or wilt despite apparently adequate water.
root-knot.progress: Knotted root galls and poor root function reduce growth and yield.
root-knot.conditions: Wash roots gently and distinguish galls from normal legume nodules.

banana-weevil.name: Banana rhizome weevil
banana-weevil.early: Plants lose vigour; holes may occur in the corm.
banana-weevil.progress: Larval tunnels weaken the corm and can cause snapping or toppling.
banana-weevil.conditions: Use clean suckers and inspect cut corm surfaces.

citrus-psyllid.name: Asian citrus psyllid
citrus-psyllid.early: Small insects and curled or distorted leaves occur on tender flush.
citrus-psyllid.progress: Nymphs and waxy deposits accumulate; the insect can spread citrus greening.
citrus-psyllid.conditions: Inspect new flush and confirm identity before selecting control.

citrus-leafminer.name: Citrus leaf miner
citrus-leafminer.early: Silvery winding mines appear in young citrus leaves.
citrus-leafminer.progress: Mined leaves distort and curl as the flush expands.
citrus-leafminer.conditions: Inspect tender flush; old hardened leaves show past injury.

rhinoceros-beetle.name: Coconut rhinoceros beetle
rhinoceros-beetle.early: Newly opened fronds show characteristic cut notches.
rhinoceros-beetle.progress: Crown boring damages young tissues and can weaken palms.
rhinoceros-beetle.conditions: Inspect the crown safely and remove breeding material around the crop.

red-palm-weevil.name: Red palm weevil
red-palm-weevil.early: Trunk or crown wounds may ooze and contain chewed fibres.
red-palm-weevil.progress: Internal larval tunnelling can cause severe crown decline or palm collapse.
red-palm-weevil.conditions: Seek prompt local inspection; internal damage can precede obvious symptoms.

coffee-berry-borer.name: Coffee berry borer
coffee-berry-borer.early: A small round hole appears near the berry tip.
coffee-berry-borer.progress: Larvae tunnel inside berries and damage the beans.
coffee-berry-borer.conditions: Inspect green and ripening berries and remove leftover infested berries.

tea-mosquito.name: Tea mosquito bug
tea-mosquito.early: Dark feeding punctures develop on tender shoots or panicles.
tea-mosquito.progress: Shoot dieback and flower or young nut injury increase.
tea-mosquito.conditions: Inspect tender flush and flowering panicles.

blossom-thrips.name: Flower thrips
blossom-thrips.early: Petals or buds show fine pale scars and small insects.
blossom-thrips.progress: Buds may distort or fail to open normally; flowers brown.
blossom-thrips.conditions: Inspect unopened buds and tap flowers over a light sheet.

lotus-aphid.name: Water-lily / plum aphid
lotus-aphid.early: Dark aphid colonies gather on emergent aquatic leaves.
lotus-aphid.progress: Sticky honeydew and distorted new growth develop.
lotus-aphid.conditions: Inspect emergent leaves; protect pond animals when considering any treatment.

sweetpotato-weevil.name: Sweet potato weevil
sweetpotato-weevil.early: Small punctures and feeding marks appear on stems or storage roots.
sweetpotato-weevil.progress: Larval tunnels develop inside roots; affected roots become unmarketable.
sweetpotato-weevil.conditions: Use clean vines and inspect roots and field residues.

sweetpotato-black-rot.name: Black rot of sweet potato
sweetpotato-black-rot.early: Dark, firm, circular spots develop on storage roots.
sweetpotato-black-rot.progress: Dark lesions enlarge; affected plants or stored roots deteriorate.
sweetpotato-black-rot.conditions: Inspect planting material and handle roots without injury.

jasmine-budworm.name: Jasmine budworm
jasmine-budworm.early: Small holes appear in unopened flower buds.
jasmine-budworm.progress: Caterpillars feed within buds, which brown or fail to open.
jasmine-budworm.conditions: Inspect unopened buds and remove infested material.

lotus-southern-blight.name: Southern blight of lotus
lotus-southern-blight.early: A published Florida record describes large leaf lesions on sacred lotus.
lotus-southern-blight.progress: The pathogen was isolated from symptomatic tissue; local confirmation is essential.
lotus-southern-blight.conditions: This is a research host record from Florida, not evidence of an outbreak in India.
